description:
`runx history <run-id> --json`.

Events come stream by stream, each stream in version order: a run and its child runs are streams of their own, and the store has no order across them. The cursor holds the last version returned for every stream of the run's tree, so a read after it never skips or repeats an event, including in child runs that started after the earlier read. `run` and `waiting` are read after the events, so they are never older than the last event returned.

cursor.description: Opaque. Pass it as `--after` to read what follows.

items.description: One event of a run's record. It carries references and digests, never outputs or secrets.

committed_at.description: When the event committed, for display only: it orders nothing.

anyOf.description: On a bounded retry; the step has not started.
On its retry after it was claimed: it reaches the world, and its effect may have happened.
On what the child run it started waits on.

outputs.description: The call's output as project artifacts of its run: one per packet output, and one for the rest.

output.description: The packet output it holds; absent on the artifact of the call's other outputs.

reason.description: Why a call that ran did not succeed.

anyOf.description: Admission refused the call; nothing ran.

role.description: The kind of agent the step asks for.

anyOf.description: A step or call waits to run again. A bounded retry (`retry_after_seconds` above zero) is runx's own: the driver that reaches it after the delay runs it. A claimed call that never settled (`retry_after_seconds` zero) runs again only on a person's acknowledgement, `{"retry": true}`, and only when it can be resent.

resend.description: Whether a claimed call can be sent again with the same input: its provider deduplicates it, or it only reads. One that cannot is never resent; its run can only be closed with the call unconfirmed.

anyOf.description: A call reached a paid runner and waits on the person's exact decision: they answer `approved` and the method they pay with (`choice`).

purchase.description: What a person decides when a call reaches a paid runner: one quote's exact offer version, seller and price, and each payment method that can pay it. The request's digest binds all of it, so an answer pays only this quote, before it expires.

methods.description: Never empty: a call no method can pay fails instead of asking.

anyOf.description: The account's runx balance, which covers the price: the price moves inside runx's ledger, with no settlement per call.
A hosted payment grant whose connector pays on the quote's network and asset.

option.description: One exact quoted option. Its provider attempt retains this binding through settlement and recovery; this is not another payment or purchase identity.

items.description: One way the buyer can pay. An answer's `choice` names it: the balance by `runx:balance`, a payment grant by the choice binding its instance and quoted option.

quote.description: The quote decided on, including its protocol-owned display terms and the exact challenge binding. An absent network is not an EVM network default.

option.description: One exact quoted option. Its provider attempt retains this binding through settlement and recovery; this is not another payment or purchase identity.
